correctness.rationale: Tree incidence surjectivity identifies the exact quotient operator as the edge matrix exponential. All generator entries yield the claimed column logarithmic norm; the exact first-order expansion and global exponential inequality follow from standard finite-dimensional matrix norm estimates. A cut signal attains the offending column to first order. Perron–Frobenius strict spectral-radius monotonicity gives path/claw classification, and degree inequalities give path/star classification. The packaged standard-library checker passed 18,248 finite tree cases and 150 rational-weight identities; finite tests are supportive only.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The theorem concerns an l1 edge-gradient seminorm of the forward vertex heat semigroup. The classical vertex-Lipschitz norm is an l-infinity edge-gradient seminorm. Their exact operator norms are generally not identical with nonuniform weights; vertex heat reversibility alone does not identify these norms. No equivalent l1 formula found in checked sources.

originality.rationale: A direct search and implication comparison found prior general Lipschitz/transport-curvature equivalences (Ollivier 2007), heat-kernel gradient bounds (Bauer et al. 2013), and tree TV optimization methods (Kolmogorov et al. 2015). None of the examined statements gives the separate edge-l1 semigroup criterion in three independently weighted arrays or the dual path/claw versus path/star positive-weight classifications. The general contraction-curvature principle is credited, not claimed as novel. An implicit antecedent remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: An implicit equivalent matrix-measure argument may exist in earlier semigroup, curvature, or signal-processing literature.

value.rationale: A natural, sharply formulated all-time weighted-BV diffusion stability problem is reduced to a local complete criterion, with an unexpectedly conductance-independent phase boundary. The two separate positive-weight topology classifications explain why freely choosing edge variation weights and freely choosing vertex masses produce distinct families of admissible trees, a structurally motivated contrast beyond simple normalized examples.
